findings.issue: Initial arrays() omitted dict-valued recurrent_states/conv_states, so fresh traces did not bind all actual GDN/conv cache tensors.
findings.required_resolution: Recursive dict/list/tuple/tensor traversal plus cache metadata and reference topology; actual GPU proof remains NOT_RUN.

findings.issue: Initial FP64 recurrence restarted each helper from actual initial_state, providing conditional one-step fidelity rather than an independent carried prefix-state oracle.
findings.required_resolution: Carry separate per-layer FP64 oracle from token0 and label dependence on actual model activations. It remains a 32-token prefix check, not an independent full-model/32K/81K proof.

findings.issue: Initial math_checks were saved only after full success. First math failure would lose token/layer/error/bound metrics while generic traceback survived.
findings.required_resolution: Persist first mathematical failure metrics and raw comparison before raising; preserve failures without retry.

findings.issue: Native normalization outputs were observed and fed to FP64 recurrence; this alone is not independent normalization validation.
findings.required_resolution: Either accurately limit qualification to post-normalization recurrence, or independently bound native normalization against frozen FP64 normalization without changing GPU math.

findings.issue: Distinct data_ptr values alone do not prove absence of overlapping persistent state views sharing a storage.
findings.required_resolution: Check actual byte-range non-overlap for all persistent GDN states or explicitly define/prove legal view layout; finite values are not a universal uninitialized-read proof.

findings.issue: Two32-token full recurrent-state traces require3GiB raw solely for GDN state, exceeding the informal2GB estimate.
findings.required_resolution: Freeze disk/raw quotas with attention/conv/logits and failure headroom, no large Mac download.

findings.issue: Initial fresh mismatch receipt recorded earliest token and metadata/hash lists, but not a decoded earliest tensor/element or numerical magnitude.
findings.required_resolution: Pure CPU comparison of retained raw bytes and dtype, first difference, max absolute/relative errors, including metadata-only differences.
